posts.title: Standard Review: Corn Kidz 64 (PC/Switch)
posts.description: So, if it wasn’t obvious by now, I love 3d collectathon platformers, and there seems to be a bit of a resurgence of these types of games in indie spaces. I just got done reviewing Cavern of Dreams , a very endearing indie title in this genre, and I decided I should revisit Corn Kidz 64 so I can finally give it the review it deserves. The short version is, I quite enjoyed it, and I definitely recommend it to fans of this type of game. That being said, it goes about its accuracy to a fault a lot of the times, and those that find Banjo-Kazooie difficult to return to may have issues with this game. Corn Kidz 64 is developed by Bogosoft, whose previous works include the 2006 freeware title Lyle in Cube Sector , which this game is billed as a successor to. This basically means that Corn Kid’z 64 was in the work for 17 years in some form or another, so hopefully it doesn’t take them as long to get to their next game. posts.title: Quick Review: Costume Quest (360/PS3/PC/IOS/Android)
posts.description: So I finally got around to checking out a game by well known game developer Tim Schafer. Tim Schafer is the founder of Double Fine productions, which produced games such as Psychonauts , Brutal Legend , as well as the remakes of Day of the Tentacle and Grim Fandango . Costume Quest is the third game made by Double Fine productions, following up the aforementioned Psychonauts and Brutal Legend . All I can say is, if those two games are as good as I heard, then Costume Quest is somewhat of an odd one out, because I did not care all that much for it. The story has you play as either a male character named Reynold, or a female character named Wren. The one you don’t choose gets kidnapped by monsters who are obsessed with candy. You get to rescue your sibling, and go trick or treating in the process.
